title: 3D Kinematic Reconstruction of the Crab Nebula That Includes the Northern Ejecta `Jet'
comment: 23 pages, 15 figures. Submitted to ApJ. Animations available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20822317
summary: We present new detailed three-dimensional kinematic reconstructions of the Crab Nebula created from hyperspectral cubes obtained with the SITELLE instrument mounted on the Canada--France--Hawaii Telescope. Our data cubes span a wavelength range from 3600Å to 7000Å, covering major emission lines including [O II] $λλ$3726, 3729, H$β$, [O III] $λλ$4959, 5007, [N II] $λ$5755, He I $λ$5876, [N II] $λλ$6548, 6584, [S II] $λλ$6717, 6731, and H$α$. The field of view encompasses the ``chimney" or ``jet," a 45-arcsec-wide funnel-shaped structure that extends 100 arcsec beyond the northern limb of the nebula. Our 3D reconstructions confirm and geometrically resolve a cavity at the jet's base that was suggested by earlier kinematic studies, establishing a direct physical connection between the filamentary network and the jet funnel. The morphology and kinematics indicate that the early pulsar wind nebula (PWN) played a central role in forming the jet. Several formation scenarios, which are not necessarily mutually exclusive, remain viable, including a bipolar outflow shaped by a circumstellar disk, a breach or underdensity in the ejecta shell, and a pre-existing progenitor mass-loss trail acting as a low-density channel. Collectively, these scenarios exhibit differing abilities to account for the jet's pronounced collimation, the absence of a southern counterpart, and its near-ballistic motion. Discriminating among them will require fully three-dimensional hydrodynamic simulations that trace the remnant's evolution from the progenitor phase through late-time PWN expansion.

AI.tldr: This study presents detailed 3D kinematic reconstructions of the Crab Nebula's jet using SITELLE hyperspectral data, revealing a cavity at the jet base and suggesting the pulsar wind nebula's key role in jet formation, with several plausible formation scenarios requiring further simulation to confirm.
AI.motivation: To understand the formation mechanisms and detailed three-dimensional kinematics of the Crab Nebula's jet structure and its connection to the surrounding filamentary network.
AI.method: Utilization of hyperspectral data cubes from the SITELLE instrument on the Canada-France-Hawaii Telescope, covering a wide wavelength range and major emission lines to reconstruct detailed 3D kinematic maps of the Crab Nebula, especially focusing on the jet and its base region.
AI.result: The 3D reconstructions confirmed and resolved a cavity at the jet's base, establishing a physical link between the jet funnel and the filamentary network. The morphology and kinematics suggest multiple viable jet formation scenarios, including influences from a bipolar outflow shaped by a circumstellar disk, ejecta shell underdensity, or a progenitor mass-loss channel.
AI.conclusion: The early pulsar wind nebula played a central role in jet formation. To definitively distinguish between competing formation scenarios, fully three-dimensional hydrodynamic simulations from progenitor to nebular phases are necessary.

title: Debiasing the Observed Fast Radio Burst Population with the CHIME/FRB Selection Function
comment: 25 pages, 10 figures, submitted to ApJ
summary: The recent release of CHIME/FRB Catalog~2 provides the largest sample to date with which to investigate the intrinsic distributions of fast radio bursts (FRBs). Leveraging an expanded campaign of 587,367 synethetic bursts injected into the live CHIME/FRB search pipeline, we perform a population analysis of the fluence, scattering timescale, pulse width, and dispersion measure distributions of Catalog~2 FRBs. We first infer the intrinsic population using a resampling-based framework that accounts for instrumental selection effects following previous CHIME/FRB population studies. A central goal of this work is to constrain the intrinsic distribution of scattering timescales, that remained weakly constrained in Catalog~1 owing to limited statistics at moderate and large scattering times ($τ\gtrsim 10\,\mathrm{ms}$ at 600~MHz) and sparse injection coverage in this regime. Second, we construct an explicit multidimensional selection function by training a logistic regression model on the injected events. This model estimates the detection probability as a function of FRB observable properties, including higher-order interaction terms. We incorporate this selection function into a simulation-based inference framework to refine the inferred intrinsic scattering-timescale distribution. We find evidence for a slight downturn in the intrinsic FRB scattering timescale distribution, though a flat or slightly rising distribution cannot be ruled out, that is further supported through a comparison with the higher-frequency scattering timescale distribution observed by Commensal Real-time ASKAP Fast Transients (CRAFT) survey.

AI.tldr: This work analyzes the largest CHIME/FRB sample with extensive injection modeling to constrain the intrinsic scattering timescale distribution of FRBs, revealing a possible slight downturn and supporting these findings through comparison with higher-frequency data from CRAFT.
AI.motivation: To better constrain the intrinsic distribution of fast radio burst (FRB) scattering timescales, which was weakly constrained in previous studies due to limited statistics and sparse injection coverage at moderate and large scattering times.
AI.method: Using the largest FRB sample from CHIME/FRB Catalog 2, the study conducted a population analysis incorporating 587,367 synthetic bursts injected into the CHIME/FRB pipeline. The authors employed a resampling-based framework accounting for instrumental selection effects, trained a logistic regression model on injections to model the selection function, and used simulation-based inference to refine the intrinsic scattering-timescale distribution.
AI.result: Evidence was found for a slight downturn in the intrinsic FRB scattering timescale distribution, although flat or slightly rising distributions could not be excluded. This finding was supported by comparisons with higher-frequency scattering timescales observed by the CRAFT survey.
AI.conclusion: The study improves constraints on the intrinsic scattering timescale distribution of FRBs by integrating a large injection set and a data-driven selection function, revealing nuanced features in the population previously unresolvable due to limited sampling and providing consistency with independent higher-frequency observations.

title: A Census of Variable and Transient Radio Sources Within High-Energy Neutrino Fields
comment: Published in Advancing Astrophysics with the SKA II (AASKAII), 2026 (arXiv:2606.20366). Report-no: AASKAII/Rosch01. Advancing Astrophysics with the SKA II (AASKAII) outlines the transformative scientific advances that will be enabled by the SKA telescopes
summary: The origin of high-energy cosmic neutrinos detected by the IceCube observatory is a hotly debated topic in astroparticle physics. Neutrinos can be produced via interactions of high-energy protons with photons. There are multiple candidate source classes which can accelerate cosmic particles to the energies required to emit high-energy cosmic neutrinos and which have in common that they lead to variable/transient radio emissions. However, so far only a few active galactic nuclei (AGNs) could be associated with high confidence with IceCube neutrinos. The bulk of the diffuse neutrino flux might be emitted from a rather faint and numerous source population. The sub-mJy low-frequency radio sky may harbor these neutrino emitters that have gone unnoticed in previous searches. SKA-Mid continuum observations of high-energy neutrino fields will yield the most complete census of coincident transient and variable radio sources that might be associated with the neutrino emission. In previous MeerKAT observations of the IceCube gold alert IC240929A at 815 MHz, we detect about 550 faint radio sources inside the 90% uncertainty region of this neutrino field with flux densities between $169\,\mathrm{μJy}$ and $140\,\mathrm{mJy}$. In its AA4 configuration, SKA-Mid will achieve about four times the sensitivity of MeerKAT, allowing for the detection of even fainter radio sources within such neutrino fields. By adding wide-field VLBI analysis of the fields under consideration, all neutrino-candidate radio sources can be tested for high brightness-temperature compact emission (indicative of an AGN classification) and milliarcsecond-scale resolved structures.

AI.tldr: This paper discusses using high-sensitivity SKA-Mid and MeerKAT observations, along with VLBI, to find faint radio sources likely associated with high-energy cosmic neutrinos detected by IceCube, aiming to uncover previously undetected neutrino emitters in the low-frequency radio sky.
AI.motivation: The origin of high-energy cosmic neutrinos detected by IceCube is uncertain, with only a few AGNs confidently linked to these neutrinos, motivating the search for fainter and numerous sources in the low-frequency radio sky.
AI.method: Using MeerKAT and SKA-Mid continuum observations of high-energy neutrino fields, combined with wide-field VLBI analysis, to detect faint radio sources and test for AGN-related compact emission and structures associated with neutrino emission.
AI.result: Detection of about 550 faint radio sources within the uncertainty region of a neutrino alert at 815 MHz with MeerKAT; SKA-Mid's higher sensitivity will enable detection of even fainter sources, facilitating a comprehensive census of transient and variable radio sources possibly linked to neutrino emission.
AI.conclusion: The combination of sensitive SKA-Mid observations and VLBI analyses can identify faint and compact radio sources potentially responsible for the diffuse high-energy cosmic neutrino flux, improving our understanding of their origin.

title: Nuclear Isomers and Their Impact on Gamma-Ray Emission in Binary Neutron Star Mergers
summary: The multi-messenger observations of GW170817 have provided strong evidence that binary neutron star mergers are a site of heavy-element production through the rapid neutron capture process. The decay of unstable $r$-process nuclei produces a significant number of $γ$-rays, which not only power the associated kilonova, but may also be observable in current and future $γ$-ray observatories, providing a direct probe of the nuclei synthesized. Current models of the emitted $γ$-rays link a nuclear reaction network with individual decay spectra. Typically, only the population of the ground state of the nuclei is tracked in the reaction network, and rapid de-excitation of the daughter nuclei is assumed when calculating the decay spectra. This may not be accurate in nuclei where there are longer-lived, high-energy nuclear isomers. In this work, we relax these assumptions, modeling the dynamic behavior of nuclear isomers for a select list of nuclei. These isomers are included as independent states in the network, with temperature-dependent effective transition rates between ground and isomeric states and $β$-feeding probabilities calculated using the nuclear level structure. We estimate the $γ$-ray flux from isomeric transitions, finding that the 743.3 keV line of Nb-97m and the 555.6 keV line of Y-91m may be detectable in $γ$-ray observatories such as COSI, AMEGO, and LOX at galactic distances. These results, calculated for a small fraction of nuclei with isomers, highlight the need for the robust inclusion of nuclear isomers in nuclear reaction networks, as well as careful modeling of the resultant $γ$-ray spectroscopy to characterize observational signals.

AI.tldr: The paper improves γ-ray emission modeling from r-process nucleosynthesis in neutron star mergers by dynamically incorporating nuclear isomers in reaction networks, predicting observable γ-ray lines from isomeric transitions, and emphasizing their importance for future γ-ray astronomy.
AI.motivation: Current modeling of γ-ray emissions from r-process nuclei in binary neutron star merger ejecta assumes population only of nuclear ground states and rapid de-excitation of daughter nuclei, which neglects the potential impact of longer-lived nuclear isomers on γ-ray spectra.
AI.method: This work models nuclear isomers dynamically by including them as independent states in the nuclear reaction network, incorporating temperature-dependent transition rates between ground and isomeric states and calculating β-feeding probabilities based on nuclear level structure for select nuclei.
AI.result: The study predicts detectable γ-ray emission lines from specific isomeric transitions (e.g., 743.3 keV line of Nb-97m and 555.6 keV line of Y-91m) in current and future γ-ray observatories like COSI, AMEGO, and LOX at galactic distances, demonstrating the significance of including nuclear isomers in reaction networks for accurate γ-ray spectroscopy.
AI.conclusion: Inclusion of nuclear isomers as independent states with dynamic transitions in nuclear reaction networks is essential for accurately modeling γ-ray emissions from r-process nuclei, enabling precise identification of observational signals and advancing multi-messenger studies of neutron star mergers.

title: Cross-correlation of SPT-3G D1 CMB lensing and DES Y3 galaxy lensing
comment: 26 pages, 14 figures
summary: Measurements of the weak lensing of galaxies and of the cosmic microwave background (CMB) provide direct probes of the cosmic matter density field, but the two observables are sensitive to different spatial scales, redshift ranges, and survey systematics. Their cross-correlation thus enables consistency checks of the theoretical model and of potential systematics in either dataset. We present measurements of the cross-correlation between CMB lensing and cosmic shear over $\sim$1,300 deg$^2$ of the sky using the SPT-3G D1 CMB lensing maps and the Dark Energy Survey Year 3 (DES Y3) shear catalogs. For the first time, we measure this cross-correlation at high significance ($\sim 14σ$) when using a polarization-only CMB lensing reconstruction that is expected to be robust against biases induced by extragalactic foregrounds. We test a variety of other CMB lensing estimators that include temperature information and exhibit different tradeoffs between foreground biases and noise, as well as a shear sample that consists of blue, star-forming galaxies and has been shown to be less impacted by galaxy intrinsic alignments. Assuming $Λ$CDM and marginalizing over uncertainties in intrinsic alignments, baryonic feedback, and various nuisance parameters, we obtain a constraint on the amplitude of matter clustering $S_8 \equiv σ_8 \sqrt{Ω_m / 0.3} = 0.833^{+0.047}_{-0.061}$, consistent with both the primary CMB results from Planck and shear-only results from DES Y3. By combining our measurement with Planck, we find mild constraints on the astrophysical processes that impact the cross-correlation. We obtain a constraint on the intrinsic alignment amplitude of the DES sample that is competitive with that from shear-only analyses, and we find a lower limit on the strength of baryonic feedback.

AI.tldr: This study measures the cross-correlation between CMB lensing and cosmic shear over 1,300 deg² using polarization-based reconstruction to avoid foreground biases, achieving a high-significance detection that supports ΛCDM cosmology and provides constraints on matter clustering and astrophysical systematic effects.
AI.motivation: To utilize the complementary sensitivities of weak lensing of galaxies and CMB lensing to perform consistency checks of cosmological models and control systematics by measuring their cross-correlation.
AI.method: Cross-correlation measurement between CMB lensing from SPT-3G D1 maps and cosmic shear from DES Year 3 shear catalogs over ~1,300 deg². Utilization of a polarization-only CMB lensing reconstruction to limit foreground biases, testing additional estimators including temperature-based reconstructions, and analyzing shear samples less affected by intrinsic alignments. Statistical inference assuming ΛCDM with marginalization over intrinsic alignments, baryonic feedback, and nuisance parameters.
AI.result: A high significance (~14σ) detection of the CMB lensing and cosmic shear cross-correlation using polarization-only data, resulting in an amplitude of matter clustering S_8=0.833^{+0.047}_{-0.061}, consistent with Planck primary CMB and DES Y3 shear-only results. Constraints on astrophysical processes like intrinsic alignments and baryonic feedback were also obtained, including competitive intrinsic alignment amplitude constraints and a lower limit on baryonic feedback strength.
AI.conclusion: The cross-correlation measurement validates the ΛCDM model consistency between galaxy weak lensing and CMB lensing probes, with robust control over foreground biases and intrinsic alignments. This approach yields competitive cosmological constraints and contributes to understanding astrophysical systematics affecting lensing measurements.

title: Hunting for extreme high-energy-peaked BL Lacs: Rare to find and difficult to classify
comment: 14 pages, 9 figures, 2 tables; accepted for publication in Journal of High Energy Astrophysics
summary:
We explore the possible existence of a new population of BL Lacs, called ultra extreme high-energy-peaked BL Lacs (UEHBLs), whose synchrotron emission component peaks in the MeV band. In particular, we analysed Swift/XRT follow-up observations of a set of 10 hard X-ray sources from the Swift/BAT catalogues which were suggested to represent the first observational hints of this new blazar population on the basis of their spectral properties.
  We find that 6 of these candidate UEHBLs can be classified as line-emitting active galactic nuclei (AGNs), 4 of which are of type 2 and X-ray absorbed objects, while 2 are type 1 AGN and X-ray unabsorbed sources. In one more case, we find that the hard X-ray emission is probably the contribution of two line-emitting AGN, i.e. a Seyfert of type 1.9 and another of type 2. All these 7 classifications exclude the possibility that these hard X-ray sources are extreme BL Lacs.
  Of the remaining 3 UEHBL candidates, only 2 objects are found to have a spectral energy distribution (SED) compatible with those expected by MeV-peaked BL Lacs: however, in one of these 2 cases, an alternative Galactic association is also possible. The third source is instead likely associated with a more classical quasi-stellar object.
  Overall, we find that UEHBLs are extremely rare to find and probably very difficult to classify. Nevertheless, they represent a viable alternative classification for hard X-ray sources displaying no obvious or very weak counterparts.

AI.tldr: This study evaluates 10 hard X-ray sources proposed as ultra extreme high-energy-peaked BL Lacs and finds that most are actually other AGN types or QSOs. Only 2 candidates potentially fit the UEHBL profile, indicating these objects are very rare and hard to definitively classify.
AI.motivation: To investigate the existence of a newly proposed population of BL Lac objects called ultra extreme high-energy-peaked BL Lacs (UEHBLs) characterized by synchrotron peaks in the MeV band.
AI.method: Analysis of Swift/XRT follow-up observations of 10 hard X-ray sources from the Swift/BAT catalogs previously suggested as candidate UEHBLs based on their spectral properties.
AI.result: Out of 10 candidates, 7 were identified as line-emitting AGNs, excluding them as UEHBLs. Only 2 remaining candidates showed spectral energy distributions consistent with MeV-peaked BL Lacs, with one having a possible alternative Galactic association; the last source resembles a classical quasi-stellar object. The study concludes UEHBLs are very rare and difficult to classify.
AI.conclusion: UEHBLs are a rare and challenging-to-identify blazar subclass, potentially accounting for some hard X-ray sources lacking clear counterparts, but many candidates previously suggested are in fact other AGN types or QSOs.

title: Cutting with precision -- Leveraging Collapse Volumes to generate the next generation of zoom-in initial conditions
comment: submitted to A&A
summary: Astrophysical processes happen across a wide range of scales. This poses a significant challenge from the perspective of modeling these processes. Modern cosmological simulations attempt to maximize the simulation volume to capture the full range of the density power spectrum while simultaneously optimizing spatial resolution for improved modeling of dynamics at galactic scales. Performing zoom-in simulations of galaxy clusters is a way to reconcile computational cost, mass resolution, and large-scale realism in simulations. To study the baryonic evolution of structures it is critical to ensure that the volume of interest is uncontaminated by high-mass particles from outside the zoom-in region. We introduce a new method of constructing stable boundaries for layered zoom-in initial conditions. Applying this method to clusters from the SLOW constrained simulation, we introduce the SLOW cluster zoom-in initial conditions. We select regions using a forward run of a gravity-only version of the parent box. We performed test simulations for a set of 20 regions created from the SLOW constrained simulations containing 30 local clusters. The simulations demonstrate these initial conditions to be stable against deformation and mixing of the boundary region. Consequently, they are uncontaminated to an unprecedented degree, reaching pristine regions of sizes exceeding 6 virial radii. These simulations will provide the basis for the first high-resolution simulations of a large set of directly comparable local galaxy cluster analogues and their environment to date. Their high fidelity in terms of stability and resolution in combination with the accuracy of the underlying local Universe model makes these simulations the first of their kind. They will enable comparisons with state-of-the art observations targeting both cluster properties and ICM physics as well as galaxy evolution in the local Universe.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a novel method for generating stable zoom-in simulation initial conditions that produce uncontaminated, high-resolution simulations of local galaxy clusters, enabling improved studies of cluster environments and galaxy evolution.
AI.motivation: Astrophysical processes span a wide range of scales, making it challenging to model them accurately. To study baryonic evolution in galaxy clusters, it is critical to ensure uncontaminated simulation volumes.
AI.method: Introduced a new method for constructing stable boundaries in layered zoom-in initial conditions, applying it to clusters from the SLOW constrained simulation, and selecting regions via a forward run of a gravity-only parent simulation.
AI.result: Test simulations of 20 regions containing 30 local clusters demonstrated that the new initial conditions maintain stable, uncontaminated boundaries extending over 6 virial radii, achieving unprecedented pristine regions.
AI.conclusion: The SLOW cluster zoom-in initial conditions enable the first high-resolution, stable, and large-scale simulations of local galaxy cluster analogues, providing a robust basis for comparisons with detailed observations of cluster properties and galaxy evolution in the local Universe.

title: Long-Period Transients as a new frontier in time-domain astronomy
comment: Published in Advancing Astrophysics with the SKA II (AASKAII), 2026 (arXiv:2606.20366) Report-no: AASKAII/Qiu01 On behalf of the SKA Transients Science Working Group
summary: Long-period radio transients (LPTs) are relatively new astrophysical objects occupying the observational gap between canonical pulsars and slowly varying radio variables. They emit coherent, highly polarised radio bursts with periods from minutes to hours, often exhibiting millisecond- to minute-scale substructure, short duty cycles, and broadband emission. Their radio luminosities typically exceed what rotational energy alone can power, necessitating alternative energy sources such as magnetic field decay, magnetospheric reconnection, or binary interactions. As multiwavelength counterparts in X-ray, optical, and infrared bands provide key constraints on progenitors and emission mechanisms, observational evidence points to a diverse progenitor population including ultra-long period magnetars and magnetic white dwarf binaries. Fast imaging surveys with SKAO and its precursors are opening a new discovery space, enabling systematic detection, high-cadence monitoring, and detailed follow-up. Despite the challenges of high extinction, intermittent emission, and computational demands for discovery, the expanding LPT population provides a new laboratory for studying coherent radio emission in a range of compact-object systems, from pulsars to white dwarf binaries. This diversity allows us to test how the emission processes depend on magnetic field strength, rotation, and binary interaction.

AI.tldr: Long-period radio transients are a newly discovered class of coherent, polarized radio sources with periods from minutes to hours, powered by mechanisms beyond rotation alone, arising from diverse progenitors like magnetars and white dwarf binaries, and are being systematically studied through advanced radio imaging surveys.
AI.motivation: To explore and characterize long-period radio transients (LPTs), which fill the observational gap between canonical pulsars and slower radio variables and exhibit unique emission properties not fully explained by known mechanisms.
AI.method: Utilization of multiwavelength observations (X-ray, optical, infrared) combined with fast imaging surveys using instruments like SKAO and its precursors for systematic detection, high-cadence monitoring, and detailed follow-up studies of LPTs.
AI.result: Identification of a diverse progenitor population including ultra-long period magnetars and magnetic white dwarf binaries, with LPTs displaying coherent, highly polarized radio bursts that require energy sources beyond rotational energy, such as magnetic field decay or binary interactions.
AI.conclusion: LPTs represent a new astrophysical laboratory that bridges canonical pulsars and other radio variables, enabling the study of coherent radio emission mechanisms influenced by magnetic field strength, rotation, and binary interactions across a variety of compact-object systems.

title: Lyman-Alpha Forest and its Cross-Correlation with High-Redshift Galaxies in Effective Field Theory at the Field Level
comment: 50 pages, 34 figures, comments welcome
summary: We present a field-level perturbative forward model for the Lyman-alpha (Lya) forest flux decrement. We validate it on two simulation suites: large-volume AbacusSummit N-body simulations with the Lya forest painted onto the dark matter field, and the Sherwood hydrodynamic simulations. Across the redshift range of the simulations (z=2.0-3.2), the 3D and 1D power spectra of the model match the simulated Lya fields at the 1% (5%) level up to k <= 0.3 (1.0) h/Mpc, with similar performance for the cross-correlation with massive dark matter halos. The counts-in-cells statistic shows excellent agreement down to cell radii of 2 Mpc/h. Leveraging cosmic variance cancellation, the model enables precision measurements of Lya bias parameters and robustly detects the full set of quadratic line-of-sight bias operators, consistent with the notion of naturalness in effective field theory (EFT). We quantify the stochasticity of the Lya forest (the analog to the one-halo term), and find it to be white (scale- and orientation-independent) on large scales, matching EFT predictions. We further find that phenomenological flux power spectrum models, based on modulations of the linear-theory power spectrum, fail at the field level even on quasi-linear scales. For the currently observing Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI), we generate large-scale clustering mocks of the Lya forest to validate cosmological parameter inference pipelines. Looking ahead to its successor, DESI-II, we produce large-volume mocks of representative samples of Lyman-break galaxies (LBGs) and Lya emitters (LAEs), calibrated on Astrid hydrodynamic simulations and matched to observations at z=3, enabling joint analyses of Lya forest and high-redshift galaxy data.

AI.tldr: A perturbative forward model for the Lyman-alpha forest flux accurately reproduces simulated flux statistics and bias parameters, validating its use for cosmological analyses and mock data generation for DESI and its successor.
AI.motivation: Develop an accurate field-level forward model for the Lyman-alpha forest flux decrement to improve cosmological analyses and parameter inference.
AI.method: Construct a perturbative forward model for the Lya flux field, validate it against large N-body and hydrodynamic simulations across relevant redshifts, and produce realistic mocks for current and future surveys.
AI.result: Model reproduces Lya flux statistics (3D/1D power spectra, counts-in-cells) within 1-5%, detects quadratic bias operators consistent with EFT, quantifies stochasticity as scale-independent, and shows phenomenological models fail at the field level; mocks enable robust cosmological inference for DESI and DESI-II.
AI.conclusion: The developed perturbative forward model provides an accurate, EFT-consistent description of the Lya forest flux, outperforms simpler models on quasi-linear scales, and supports precise cosmological parameter estimation through realistic mock data generation.

title: A Boundary-Consistent Two-Zone Electron Kernel for Distant Pulsar Contributions to Positron Flux and Anisotropy
comment: submitted
summary:
We present a semi-analytical series solution for electron and positron propagation in a spherical two-zone diffusion model. The solution treats slow diffusion inside a near-source region and standard interstellar diffusion outside it, while synchrotron and Klein--Nishina inverse-Compton cooling are included through energy characteristics. The formulation avoids the oscillatory cancellations of direct two-zone integral evaluations and preserves the sharp radiative cooling boundary seen in finite-volume checks.
  We apply the kernel to pulsar contributions to the local cosmic-ray lepton flux. Nearby pulsars remain natural candidates near the TeV cutoff, but at tens to hundreds of GeV the larger source volume allows more distant pulsars to contribute collectively: for a disk half-thickness of $0.2\,{\rm kpc}$, sources beyond $1\,{\rm kpc}$ can still provide $37$--$47\%$ of the $10$--$100\,{\rm GeV}$ flux. Comparing with AMS-02 positron data and all-electron anisotropy limits, and imposing an inner $100\,{\rm pc}$ cavity motivated by the Local Bubble and pulsar proper motions, we find that Geminga-scale slow-diffusion halos remain compatible with current data. The fitted pulsar component is dominated by sources beyond $0.3\,{\rm kpc}$, but flux and anisotropy data alone do not uniquely determine the halo size; external information such as TeV halo morphology is still required.

AI.tldr: This study develops a semi-analytical model for electron/positron propagation using a two-zone diffusion approach including radiative cooling, finds significant pulsar contributions to local cosmic-ray fluxes from both near and distant sources, and shows compatibility with current observational data but emphasizes the need for additional morphological constraints to fully determine diffusion halo characteristics.
AI.motivation: To develop a robust solution for modeling electron and positron propagation considering different diffusion regimes and cooling effects near cosmic-ray sources, addressing limitations of integral evaluations and capturing radiative boundaries accurately.
AI.method: Derived a semi-analytical series solution for a spherical two-zone diffusion model incorporating slow diffusion near sources and standard diffusion in the interstellar medium, including energy losses from synchrotron and Klein-Nishina inverse-Compton cooling, avoiding oscillatory cancellations in integral evaluations.
AI.result: The model successfully explains local cosmic-ray lepton flux contributions from pulsars, showing that distant pulsars beyond 1 kpc contribute significantly at tens to hundreds of GeV energies. It matches AMS-02 positron data and anisotropy limits, supporting slow-diffusion halos like Geminga within current constraints, while highlighting the need for additional data to resolve halo size ambiguities.
AI.conclusion: The presented semi-analytical solution effectively models two-zone diffusion with cooling for cosmic-ray leptons, affirming the role of both nearby and distant pulsars in observed fluxes and indicating that current data are insufficient to uniquely constrain halo parameters without external observational inputs.

title: First full-shape joint analysis of the two- and three-point correlation functions on real data: $Λ$CDM cosmological constraints from BOSS DR12
comment: 19 pages, 12 figures. Submitted to A&A
summary: The three-point correlation function (3PCF) encodes cosmological information beyond the two-point correlation function (2PCF), yet a full-shape joint analysis in redshift space using real data has so far been lacking. We present the first full-shape cosmological constraints from a joint analysis of 2PCF and 3PCF in redshift space, using BOSS DR12 data, extending to real data, including Alcock--Paczyński and redsfhit space distortions, the full-shape configuration-space framework validated in real space for the first time by Euclid Collaboration: Guidi et al (2026). We model both statistics adopting the velocity difference generating function (VDG) framework, incorporating non-perturbative Fingers-of-God damping, a complete Eulerian galaxy bias expansion, and infrared resummation. Fast and accurate theoretical predictions are obtained using dedicated emulators, which enable a full-shape likelihood analysis of the 3PCF and its combination with the 2PCF, varying the cosmological parameters $10^9 A_s, ω_{\rm cdm}$ and $h$, while the baryon fraction density $ω_{b}$ is fixed to its fiducial value. The covariance matrix is estimated from 2048 MultiDark-Patchy mocks, and an optimal data-vector compression ensures a stable covariance inversion. The perturbative model is validated against goodness-of-fit tests across different scales, and provides a good description of the joint data vector down to $r_{\rm min}^{\rm 3PCF} \sim 60\,h^{-1}{\rm Mpc}$. We find that the joint 2PCF+3PCF analysis yields significant improvements over the 2PCF-only baseline, with gains of approximately 29\%, 10\%, and 24\% on $σ(h)$, $σ(ω_{\rm cdm})$, and $σ(A_s)$, respectively. The improvements mainly arise from the additional BAO cosmological information encoded in the 3PCF triangle configurations.

AI.tldr: This paper presents the first joint full-shape 2PCF and 3PCF cosmological analysis in redshift space on real data, showing significant improvements in parameter constraints by leveraging additional cosmological information encoded in the 3PCF from BOSS DR12 observations.
AI.motivation: To extend cosmological analyses beyond the two-point correlation function by including the three-point correlation function in redshift space, thereby capturing additional cosmological information previously unexploited in real data analyses.
AI.method: We performed a joint full-shape likelihood analysis of the 2PCF and 3PCF in redshift space using BOSS DR12 data, modeling both with the velocity difference generating function framework, incorporating non-perturbative effects, galaxy bias expansions, and infrared resummation. Predictions were accelerated by emulators, and covariance matrices estimated from 2048 mocks with optimal data compression to ensure stable inversion.
AI.result: The joint 2PCF+3PCF analysis improved constraints by approximately 29% for the Hubble parameter uncertainty, 10% for cold dark matter density uncertainty, and 24% for the amplitude of primordial fluctuations, driven primarily by the BAO information in the 3PCF configurations.
AI.conclusion: The joint full-shape analysis of the two-point and three-point correlation functions in redshift space significantly enhances cosmological parameter constraints compared to using the two-point function alone, demonstrating the 3PCF's value in extracting additional cosmological information, especially from BAO features.

title: The Emerging Population of High-energy Emitting Radio Galaxies
comment: Published in Advancing Astrophysics with the SKA II (AASKAII), 2026 (arXiv:2606.20366). Report-no: AASKAII/Bruni01. Advancing Astrophysics with the SKA II (AASKAII) outlines the transformative scientific advances that will be enabled by the SKA telescopes
summary: High-energy emission from radio galaxies provides a unique laboratory to study the connection between accretion, jet formation, and particle acceleration in active galactic nuclei (AGN). The recent detection of $γ$-ray emission from misaligned radio galaxies - including Compact Symmetric Objects (CSOs), FR0, FRI/II, and even Giant Radio Galaxies (GRGs) - has shown that efficient particle acceleration is not limited to blazars, but occurs throughout the full radio-loud AGN population. This finding supports a unifying framework where leptonic synchrotron, synchrotron self-Compton (SSC), and external inverse-Compton (EIC) processes coexist across multiple spatial scales, from the inner jet and corona to the extended lobes, possibly with a hadronic contribution in dense environments. The Square Kilometre Array (SKA) will be pivotal in advancing this field. SKA1-Low will detect and characterize diffuse, low-surface-brightness emission tracing aged plasma and jet duty cycles. SKA1-Mid will enable high-resolution spectral and polarimetric studies of compact jets and nuclear regions, while SKA-VLBI will connect parsec- to kiloparsec-scale structures, identifying the exact sites of high-energy dissipation. In synergy with forthcoming high-energy missions such as NewAthena and CTAO, SKA will provide the first spatially resolved, multi-scale view of particle acceleration and energy release in misaligned AGN, unveiling the physical link between the central engine and its large-scale feedback on the host galaxy evolution.

AI.tldr: The paper highlights how γ-ray emissions from diverse radio galaxies reveal widespread particle acceleration, and emphasizes the critical role of the SKA and upcoming missions in resolving jet structures and feedback processes in AGN.
AI.motivation: To understand the connection between accretion, jet formation, and particle acceleration in active galactic nuclei through high-energy emission from radio galaxies.
AI.method: Observational analysis of γ-ray emissions from various types of misaligned radio galaxies combined with multi-wavelength techniques including leptonic synchrotron, SSC, and EIC processes across multiple spatial scales; utilizing the capabilities of the Square Kilometre Array (SKA) alongside forthcoming high-energy missions.
AI.result: Efficient particle acceleration occurs across the entire radio-loud AGN population, not just blazars, with evidence supporting a unifying framework involving multiple radiative processes and spatial scales. SKA will enable detection and characterization of aged plasma, compact jets, and the precise sites of high-energy dissipation, providing a multi-scale spatially resolved picture of AGN.
AI.conclusion: The study establishes that high-energy particle acceleration is a widespread phenomenon in radio-loud AGN, and the integration of SKA with new high-energy observatories will revolutionize understanding of the interplay between AGN central engines and their large-scale feedback on galaxy evolution.

title: Supernova remnants in the new radio astronomy era
comment: Published in Advancing Astrophysics with the SKAII (AASKAII), 2026(arXiv:2606.20366). Report-no: AASKAII/Ingallinera01
summary: Supernova remnants (SNRs) are what is left after stellar explosions, when the stellar ejecta, the explosion shock and the circumstellar medium interact. Despite being among the first objects studied in radio astronomy, observational difficulties have so far prevented a definitive characterisation, which would help answer open questions related to these sources. It is debated which is the contribution of SNRs to Galactic cosmic rays, or how the interaction with the surrounding environments influences the particle energetics. The SKA precursors are providing valuable and unexpected discoveries on SNRs, thanks to their unique capabilities to probe spatial scales from a few arcseconds to a few degrees with a sensitivity of tens of microjansky. Accurate integrated flux density measurements and arcsecond-scale spectral-index maps are now possible for tens of SNRs, substantially expanding the small subset of remnants traditionally studied in great detail. SKA will markedly enhance current observations by providing: higher sensitivity, enabling the detection of fainter SNRs also in polarisation, revealing diffuse structures and the underlying magnetic field configuration; higher angular resolution, allowing detailed mapping of compact remnants and reducing depolarisation in fine structures, tracing filaments and shocks fronts; wider frequency coverage to probe unexplored spectral windows, where spectral turnovers and breaks or cut-off may occur, establishing a direct connection to X-ray and γ-ray emission that constrains the electron population, and enabling accurate modelling of the non-thermal emission across the electromagnetic spectrum; improved image fidelity for more reliable cross-matching with other wavelengths, leading to a better understanding of the SNR-interstellar medium interplay.

AI.tldr: SKA precursors and the SKA will revolutionize SNR studies by enabling high-sensitivity, high-resolution, and wide-frequency radio observations, leading to better understanding of their role in cosmic ray production and interstellar medium interactions.
AI.motivation: To address unresolved questions about supernova remnants (SNRs), including their role in Galactic cosmic rays and the influence of their environments on particle energetics, which has been hindered by observational limitations.
AI.method: Utilization of SKA precursors and the upcoming SKA's advanced capabilities, such as improved sensitivity, angular resolution, frequency coverage, and image fidelity to conduct detailed radio observations of SNRs at multiple spatial scales and frequencies.
AI.result: SKA precursors have already enabled the detection and detailed study of more SNRs with arcsecond-scale spectral-index maps and integrated flux density measurements. The SKA will further enhance these studies by detecting fainter SNRs, resolving fine structures, tracing magnetic fields, exploring new spectral windows, and improving cross-wavelength comparisons.
AI.conclusion: The SKA and its precursors will significantly advance the characterization of SNRs, providing deeper insights into their physical properties, particle acceleration mechanisms, and interactions with the interstellar medium, which were previously limited by observational constraints.

title: The SKA View of the Sunyaev-Zeldovich Effect from Massive Cosmic Halos
